explanation: Use 'a/an' before professions: She is a doctor.
Use 'an' before vowel sounds: I ate an apple.
Use 'a/an' when mentioning something for the first time: I bought a new car.
Use 'an' before silent h: Wait an hour.
Use 'a' before /juː/ sound: She goes to a university.
Use 'an' before vowel sounds: Take an umbrella.
Use 'a' for singular countable nouns: That's a good idea.
Use 'the' for things unique in context: The sun is bright.
Use 'the' when both speaker and listener know which one: Close the door.
Use 'the' with superlatives: She is the best student.
Use 'the' with ordinals: Go to the second floor.
Use 'the' for unique things: The moon is full tonight.
Use 'the' with 'same': We have the same answer.
No article before meals: I have breakfast at 8.
No article before sports: They play football.
No article in fixed expressions: I'm at home.
No article in 'go to bed': Time to go to bed.
No article for uncountable nouns in general: Water is essential.
No article when referring to the purpose: She goes to school.
No article before languages: I speak English.
